Order 
The appeal was heard and reserved for judgment on 07/03/2025.
2. This Misc. Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed for enhancement of compensation by Rs.4,75,000/-.

3. Learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal/Special District Judge, Mandla in Claim Case No.33/2005 (Chameli Bai vs Beran @ Verendra and others) vide award dated 07/11/2006 awarded a compensation of Rs.9000/- to the claimant Chameli Bai aged about 4 years through guardian Chhotelal Jhariya for a motor accident dated 30/04/2005.

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.9000/- only along with interest and affixed the liability on non-applicant No.2 Ravi Prasad Bairagi/ NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:25664 2 MA-144-2007 owner of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.MP/51/B/4563.
He further submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is o n lower side and prayed that the compensation may be enhanced.
5. At the time of hearing, it was submitted by learned counsel for appellant that the disability certificate (Ex.P/2) has been disbelieved by the Tribunal in spite of evidence of doctor (PW-2).

The Disability Certificate was issued by Dr. R. K. Shrivastava, Orthopedic Specialist, Government Hospital, Mandla wherein it is stated that disability is of 18% and it is further stated that he has Chameli Bai vs Beran @ Verendra on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130345484/
1 examined the patient on 30/11/2005 and the father and mother of the injured stated him that her daughter met with an accident.

6. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record.
7.
On perusal of the record, it is seen that learned Tribunal in its judgment in para -19 has referred to the evidence of Dr. R. K. Shrivastava (PW-2).
In para-26, learned Tribunal has mentioned that three is no photo of injured in Disability Certificate (Ex.P/2), but only on this ground it cannot be stated that certificate Ex.P/2 is forged.
In para-27, it is held that it is proved that applicant Chameli Bai sustained fracture but permanent disability is not proved.

It is seen that no proper reasoning regarding disbelieving of the Disability Certificate has been given by the Tribunal as per Section 142 of MV Act (As stood before date of repealing i.e. on 01/09/2019) therefore, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:25664 3 MA-144-2007 there is an error in award of learned Tribunal.
Accordingly, finding regarding permanent disability is set aside and it is held that minor girl sustained permanent disability to the extent of 18%.
8.

Therefore, on overall consideration of the matter as also on account of permanent disability of 18% and on the other head i.e. future treatment, pain and suffering, special died, attendant expenses, this Court is of the view that on a lumpsum basis amount of compensation can be increased/enhanced in the interest of justice.

9. Considering the argument of learned counsel for the appellant and keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, in considered opinion of this Court, compensation amount is enhanced on lumpsum basis by Rs.3,00,000/-.
10. Needless to say that rate of interest and other terms and conditions shall be as per the impugned award.
11. Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed of.
